perspective:
From Gloria Bangura’s perspective:

- I work as an administrative assistant at a large event planning company; Donald Ortega is a part-time bartender during company events. We’re colleagues but not personally close.
- Over several events, I noticed Donald seemed distracted and unenthusiastic while serving drinks.
- I approached him and asked if everything was okay with the job. He told me he wasn’t “as into it” as he used to be and that it felt “kind of repetitive.”
- After that conversation, I started thinking his job dissatisfaction might point to something deeper. I suggested he consider talking to a professional about it.
- He said he hadn’t really considered that and wasn’t sure it would help.
- After that, I sensed a shift in Donald’s behavior toward me and worried he resented my suggestion or felt I had overstepped.
- I apologized and explained I only wanted to help because I cared. He said he was “a bit taken aback at first” but knew I meant well and that it was “a lot to process.”
- I felt relieved that the tension had eased, and I wanted to strengthen our working relationship.
- I invited him to collaborate on an upcoming project, saying it could use his creative input. He accepted and said it sounded like a great opportunity.
- During the collaboration, I observed Donald making significant contributions and showing renewed enthusiasm. I came to see him as a valuable team member.
- During a team meeting, I publicly acknowledged his work, saying his efforts were crucial to the project’s success. He thanked me and said it felt great to be appreciated.
